topics.mining: Torches drop themselves when broken by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Place this torch on a suitable support for steady light. It does not need fuel after placement or redstone power.
topics.redstone: This light torch does not supply redstone power or switch off when powered. Use a redstone torch for a circuit component.

topics.operation: Place this torch on a suitable support for steady light. It does not need fuel after placement or redstone power.
topics.redstone: This light torch does not supply redstone power or switch off when powered. Use a redstone torch for a circuit component.

topics.operation: Place this torch on a suitable support for steady light. It does not need fuel after placement or redstone power.
topics.redstone: This light torch does not supply redstone power or switch off when powered. Use a redstone torch for a circuit component.

topics.mining: Lanterns drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Place a lantern on top of a support or hang it below one. It gives steady light without fuel or power.
topics.redstone: This lantern is always lit. Redstone power does not toggle it; use a redstone lamp or copper bulb for controlled lighting.

topics.mining: Lanterns drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Place a lantern on top of a support or hang it below one. It gives steady light without fuel or power.
topics.redstone: This lantern is always lit. Redstone power does not toggle it; use a redstone lamp or copper bulb for controlled lighting.

topics.mining: End rods drop themselves by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.location: Find end rods in End cities, or craft them from blaze rods and popped chorus fruit.
topics.operation: End rods are steady light sources that can be placed in different orientations. They do not need redstone power.

topics.mining: Use Silk Touch to collect the campfire itself. Without Silk Touch it drops 2 charcoal, along with items cooking on it. An axe is fastest.
topics.operation: Place up to 4 raw food items on a lit campfire to cook without adding fuel. Extinguish it with a shovel or water, and relight it with flint and steel or another suitable ignition method.
topics.water: Water extinguishes the campfire. A waterlogged campfire cannot be lit until its water is removed.
topics.fire: A lit campfire hurts entities standing on it. It cooks food without being consumed and does not spread fire to surrounding blocks.

topics.mining: Use Silk Touch to collect the campfire itself. Without Silk Touch it drops soul soil, along with items cooking on it. An axe is fastest.
topics.operation: Place up to 4 raw food items on a lit campfire to cook without adding fuel. Extinguish it with a shovel or water, and relight it with flint and steel or another suitable ignition method.
topics.water: Water extinguishes the campfire. A waterlogged campfire cannot be lit until its water is removed.
topics.fire: A lit campfire hurts entities standing on it. It cooks food without being consumed and does not spread fire to surrounding blocks.

topics.mining: A beacon drops itself when broken by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Build a pyramid of iron, gold, emerald, diamond or netherite blocks under the beacon and keep a clear beam path to the sky. Open it, select an unlocked effect and pay an accepted mineral item to activate the selection.
topics.location: Craft a beacon using a Nether star from the Wither, glass and obsidian.
topics.redstone: Beacons do not need redstone power. Their activation depends on a valid mineral pyramid and unobstructed beam; copper blocks cannot power the pyramid.

topics.mining: A conduit drops itself by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Surround the conduit with water and build a valid frame of prismarine variants or sea lanterns. At least 16 frame blocks activate Conduit Power; larger valid frames extend its range. It helps wet players breathe, see and mine underwater.
topics.water: The conduit needs the surrounding 3-by-3-by-3 space filled with water. Its frame sits outside that central water space. A dry conduit does not grant Conduit Power.
topics.location: Craft a conduit from a heart of the sea and 8 nautilus shells.

topics.mining: Use a diamond or netherite pickaxe to collect a respawn anchor. It loses its stored glowstone charges when broken. Weaker tools drop nothing.
topics.operation: In the Nether, add glowstone to charge a respawn anchor, then use it to set your respawn point. Respawning consumes a charge; keep it charged and leave safe space nearby. Using a charged anchor outside the Nether makes it explode.
topics.redstone: A comparator reads the charge level. Redstone power alone does not recharge the anchor; it needs glowstone.
topics.danger: Using a charged respawn anchor outside the Nether causes a dangerous explosion. Use a bed for ordinary Overworld respawning instead.

topics.mining: Beds drop themselves by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use a bed in the Overworld at night or during a thunderstorm to sleep when conditions permit. Using it can set your respawn point; leave safe room around it. Never try to sleep in one in the Nether or the End; it explodes there.
topics.danger: Trying to sleep in a bed in the Nether or the End causes a dangerous explosion. Use a charged respawn anchor for Nether respawning instead.

topics.mining: Sponges drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a hoe is fastest.
topics.location: Look in ocean monument sponge rooms and obtain wet sponges from elder guardians, then dry them.
topics.water: A dry sponge absorbs nearby water and becomes a wet sponge. It cannot keep absorbing indefinitely; dry it before using it again.

topics.mining: Wet sponges drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a hoe is fastest.
topics.location: Find wet sponges in some ocean monument sponge rooms or from elder guardians.
topics.water: Wet sponges cannot absorb more water. Dry one in a furnace, or place it in the Nether to dry it instantly.

topics.mining: Rails drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Ordinary rails guide minecarts and can form curves and slopes. They do not accelerate a cart by themselves.
topics.redstone: Ordinary rails are not boosters or power sources. Power can affect which way certain rail junctions connect.

topics.mining: Rails drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Powered rails accelerate minecarts while powered and brake carts when unpowered. They do not form curves.
topics.redstone: Supply redstone power to enable acceleration. Powered rails can pass power along a limited connected run; longer tracks need more power sources.

topics.mining: Rails drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Detector rails emit redstone power while a minecart is on them. Use them as track sensors rather than as powered-rail boosters.
topics.redstone: A minecart activates the detector rail. A comparator can read compatible minecart cargo when the cart is on the detector.

topics.mining: Rails drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Powered activator rails trigger special minecart behavior, such as ejecting passengers, priming TNT minecarts or disabling hopper-minecart collection.
topics.redstone: Redstone power enables the rail activation effect. It does not speed carts up; use powered rails for acceleration.

topics.mining: This block drops itself by hand or with any tool; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Place ladders against a suitable vertical support. Move into the ladder to climb; sneaking lets you hold position.

topics.mining: Scaffolding breaks instantly and drops itself. Removing support can make connected scaffolding collapse.
topics.operation: Use scaffolding as a temporary climbable building platform. Jump to climb and sneak to descend. Build outward from supported scaffolding, respecting its support limit.
topics.gravity: Unsupported scaffolding falls or collapses. Breaking a base can bring down dependent scaffolding above and beside it.

topics.mining: Use shears to collect the cobweb block. A sword without Silk Touch gives 1 string instead. Most other ordinary tools drop nothing.
topics.location: Find cobwebs in places such as abandoned mineshafts, abandoned villages and stronghold libraries.
topics.operation: Cobwebs slow entities that move through them, including falling entities. Use them for traps or collect them for string.

topics.mining: Slime blocks drop themselves instantly by hand or with any tool.
topics.operation: Slime blocks bounce entities landing on them unless the bounce is suppressed, such as by sneaking. They also stick to compatible neighboring blocks when moved by pistons.
topics.redstone: Pistons can move attached compatible blocks with a slime block, subject to piston limits and immovable blocks. Slime blocks do not stick to honey blocks.

topics.mining: Honey blocks drop themselves instantly by hand or with any tool.
topics.operation: Honey blocks slow movement and jumping, cushion falls and let entities slide down their sides. They can carry compatible blocks in piston mechanisms.
topics.redstone: Honey blocks stick to compatible neighboring blocks when moved by a piston. They do not stick to slime blocks, so the two can be used in adjacent moving sections.

topics.mining: Honeycomb blocks drop themselves by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Honeycomb blocks are decorative blocks made from honeycomb. They are not sticky honey blocks and cannot be unpacked into honeycomb.

topics.mining: Unprimed TNT normally drops itself when broken by hand or with a tool. Ignition or an explosion primes it instead of collecting it.
topics.operation: Ignite TNT using an appropriate ignition method or redstone power. Once primed it becomes a timed explosive, so move to safety.
topics.redstone: Redstone power primes TNT. Removing power afterward does not cancel its fuse.
topics.danger: TNT explosions can hurt entities and destroy blocks. Water changes how block damage works, but it does not make standing beside an explosion safe.

topics.mining: A monster spawner cannot be collected in normal Survival, even with Silk Touch. A pickaxe destroys it for experience; it does not drop a spawner item.
topics.location: Find monster spawners in structures such as monster rooms, mineshafts, Nether fortresses and strongholds.
topics.operation: An ordinary monster spawner needs a nearby player and valid space and conditions for its configured mob. Keep or disable it in place; you cannot pick it up with Silk Touch.

topics.mining: Trial spawners drop nothing, even with Silk Touch. Do not break one if you want to use its encounters again.
topics.location: Find trial spawners in trial chambers underground in the Overworld.
topics.operation: Approach a trial spawner to start a limited mob encounter. Defeat its mobs for rewards, then wait for its cooldown. Ominous trials have additional conditions and rewards.

topics.mining: Vaults drop nothing when broken, even with Silk Touch. They cannot be collected normally in Survival.
topics.operation: Use the appropriate trial key on a vault to claim your reward. Ordinary vaults use trial keys; ominous vaults need ominous trial keys. Each player can unlock a particular vault only once.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Ring a bell to alert nearby villagers to seek shelter at the appropriate times. During a raid it can also help reveal nearby raiders.
topics.redstone: A redstone signal can ring a bell. You can also strike it manually or with suitable projectiles.

topics.mining: Use Silk Touch to collect the chiseled bookshelf itself. Without Silk Touch only the stored books drop; an axe is fastest.
topics.storage: A chiseled bookshelf holds 6 books, including ordinary books, written books, books and quills, and enchanted books.
topics.operation: Use an individual slot to insert or remove a book. Unlike ordinary bookshelves, chiseled bookshelves do not boost an enchanting table.
topics.redstone: A comparator reads which bookshelf slot was most recently interacted with, not how many books are stored.

topics.mining: This block drops itself by hand or with any tool; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary. Stored items also drop.
topics.storage: A shelf displays up to 3 item stacks. It is a quick-access display, not a 27-slot chest.
topics.operation: Use a shelf to place, remove or swap displayed items. Powered connected shelves provide quick hotbar swapping.
topics.redstone: Power enables shelf hotbar-swapping behavior. Adjacent compatible shelves can form a connected group for swapping more hotbar slots.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use this block for decorative supports, grilles or barriers. It is not a redstone power source.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use this block for decorative supports, grilles or barriers. It is not a redstone power source.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use these copper blocks for decorative building. Their appearance depends on oxidation stage.
topics.water: This copper building block can be waterlogged.
topics.oxidation: Unwaxed copper oxidizes over time. Apply honeycomb to preserve its current stage, or scrape oxidation back with an axe.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use these copper blocks for decorative building. Their appearance depends on oxidation stage.
topics.water: This copper building block can be waterlogged.
topics.oxidation: Waxed copper keeps its current oxidation stage. An axe removes wax, then can scrape oxidation back one stage per use.

topics.operation: Use these copper blocks for decorative building. Their appearance depends on oxidation stage.
topics.water: This copper building block can be waterlogged.
topics.oxidation: Unwaxed copper oxidizes over time. Apply honeycomb to preserve its current stage, or scrape oxidation back with an axe.

topics.operation: Use these copper blocks for decorative building. Their appearance depends on oxidation stage.
topics.water: This copper building block can be waterlogged.
topics.oxidation: Waxed copper keeps its current oxidation stage. An axe removes wax, then can scrape oxidation back one stage per use.

topics.mining: Use a stone pickaxe or better to collect a lightning rod. Weaker tools drop nothing.
topics.operation: Place a lightning rod to attract nearby lightning strikes to its tip. Give the strike a safe landing area; a rod does not prevent every kind of fire hazard.
topics.redstone: A lightning strike produces a brief redstone signal from the rod.
topics.oxidation: Unwaxed lightning rods oxidize over time. Honeycomb preserves the stage and an axe can scrape oxidation back.

topics.mining: Use a stone pickaxe or better to collect a lightning rod. Weaker tools drop nothing.
topics.operation: Place a lightning rod to attract nearby lightning strikes to its tip. Give the strike a safe landing area; a rod does not prevent every kind of fire hazard.
topics.redstone: A lightning strike produces a brief redstone signal from the rod.
topics.oxidation: Waxed lightning rods preserve their oxidation stage. Remove wax with an axe before scraping oxidation.

topics.mining: Wooden slabs, stairs and fences drop themselves when broken by hand or with any tool; an axe is fastest.
topics.operation: Use this wooden shape for building. It does not fall when unsupported.
topics.water: Single wooden slabs, stairs and fences can be waterlogged.

topics.mining: A double wooden slab drops 2 matching slabs when broken, not one double-slab item. An axe is fastest. Silk Touch does not keep it as a double slab.
topics.operation: Use this wooden shape for building. It does not fall when unsupported.
topics.water: A double slab cannot be waterlogged.
